correctness.rationale: The numerical iff and the specified witness are correct under the stated toric criterion. In the quotient convention K_Y=-2ξ+π*(K_B+L), with restrictions K_B±L on the two sections. The effective cone generated by S,F gives the two strict products. For the vertical surface over C, K_Y has negative fiber degree; the inverse section count is a sum over j=0,…,2n with summand max(0,1+jℓ−n(k+ℓ)), where k=K_B·C and ℓ=L·C. The normalized linear term on [0,2] has maximum |ℓ|−k; positivity on an interval gives quadratic growth, otherwise the count is at most linear. Only the surface over S gives an extra condition. The curve degrees over S are m−2±(b−am); the other section-curve degrees are already nonzero by the products, and the four ruling fibers have degree −2. The full anticanonical polytope contains a neighborhood of zero, and points impose no constraint. At (2,3,5) the products are 1 and 45 and |b−am|=1; K_B+L=S+F and −(K_B−L)=5S+9F has intersection −1 with S, so neither orientation meets the anti-ampleness hypothesis. The word 'first' has no specified ordering and is not supported as a priority or minimality assertion: if it means smallest m, (1,6,4) is an earlier parameter witness (the products are 4 and 56, |b−a|=2, and the two tests of anti-ampleness fail). The attached rational fan check is finite corroboration, not the proof, and was inspected rather than run.
